metadata.case_name: MAK PO LING v. YOUNG YAU YAU CECILIA

injuries.description: six impacted teeth on her upper jaw
source: what is the particular dental condition of this patient is that she had six impacted teeth on her upper jaw.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of teeth or supporting structures

source: finding 11 said, “There were evidence of generalised root resorption”
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of hard dental tissues and pulp

source: finding 12, “Evidence of interproximal ... alveolar bone loss.”
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of periodontal tissues

injuries.description: extraction of three lower teeth including the lower left first bicuspid (tooth 34), removal of the bridge pontic at tooth 45 (the lower right second bicuspid) and extraction of the lower right first molar (tooth 46)
source: Three of my lower teeth were removed in the course of the orthodontic treatment. The lower left first bicuspid, (tooth 34), and the bridge pontic at tooth 45, (the lower right second bicuspid) were removed at the initial stage of the orthodontic treatment. The lower right first molar, (tooth 46) were later removed in March 2005.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

injuries.description: gingival recession, exposing roots of the teeth
source: her teeth are sensitive to hot and cold (due to gingival recession, exposing roots of the teeth)
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of periodontal tissues

injuries.description: spacings between the remaining teeth (wider than usual)
source: because of three teeth being removed from her lower jaw, generally, the space between the remaining teeth are wider than usual.
Food get caught between teeth after eating (due to spacings between teeth)
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

injuries.description: unstable occlusion and premature occlusal contact
source: Miss Mak still complains that her lower jaw slides before coming to a halt when biting down (due to unstable occlusion and prematureocclusal contact).

manifestations.description: ulcer of gum, causing serious pain
inarticulate and could not discharge her responsibility properly as a flight attendant, including but not limited to the making of announcements to passengers
serious loss of appetite and weight
unable to chew up food effectively and efficiently (due to poor occlusion)
teeth sensitive to hot and cold (due to gingival recession, exposing roots of the teeth)
food gets caught between teeth after eating (due to spacings between teeth)
lower jaw slides before coming to a halt when biting down (due to unstable occlusion and prematureocclusal contact)
lost self-confidence; has to constantly restrain herself from showing her front teeth when laughing
premature occlusal contact / unstable occlusion (clinical finding)

treatments_received.treatment: orthodontic treatment by the Defendant (Dr Young) from June 2004 to June 2005
source: The actual orthodontic treatment began in June and ended in June 2005, when I began to have serious doubts about Dr Young’s competence to properly discharge her task, despite her repeated reassurance that the orthodontic treatment was in good progress.

treatments_received.treatment: extraction of teeth (three lower teeth: tooth 34, bridge pontic 45, tooth 46)
source: Three of my lower teeth were removed in the course of the orthodontic treatment. The lower left first bicuspid, (tooth 34), and the bridge pontic at tooth 45, (the lower right second bicuspid) were removed at the initial stage of the orthodontic treatment. The lower right first molar, (tooth 46) were later removed in March 2005.

treatments_received.treatment: remedial orthodontic treatment by Dr Leung from September 2005 to February 2009 (41 months); removal of orthodontic appliance; upper removable retainer and lower free fixed retainer prescribed
source: After 41 months from September 2005 to February 2009 of remedial treatment, he eventually removed Miss Mak’s orthodontic appliance and prescribed an upper removable retainer and a lower free fixed retainer for her.

treatments_future.treatment: future dental/orthodontic treatment to restore masticatory function or aim for optimum esthetics and function (cost estimate $40,000 to $60,000)
source: In my view, there can be two options to rectify, or at least to alleviate, [the Plaintiff’s] existing problems as mentioned above. Depending on the Plaintiff’s treatment objectives, option 1 is to restore or to improve [the Plaintiff’s] existing masticatory functions only. Option 2 is to aim for an optimum result which is esthetics and functions.
the doctor said the treatment price would range from $40,000 to $60,000.

losses.description: wedding banquet cancelled and unsatisfactory orthodontic condition seriously lowered her self-esteem; lost self-confidence
became inarticulate and could not discharge her responsibility properly as a flight attendant, including but not limited to the making of announcements to passengers

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy food and drink
losses.description: unable to chew up food effectively and efficiently; had to cut food into small pieces and swallow without chewing; suffered serious loss of appetite and weight
removal/extraction of three lower teeth and generalised root resorption and alveolar bone loss affecting the dentition

comparable_cases.injury_description: Unsuccessful orthodontic treatment to an airline attendant with complaints similar to present case
